question: Should OpenClaw accept `{ owner }` records as a persisted `plugins.slots.memory` and `plugins.slots.contextEngine` config contract in core?
rationale: The implementation changes a public config shape and auth/startup semantics; automation can identify defects, but maintainers must decide whether this closed-stale RFC direction should become supported product API.

options.title: Sponsor after repair
options.body: Keep the direction open, but require a rebase, the listed source fixes, exact-head proof, and explicit maintainer acceptance before merge.

options.title: Pause behind the RFC
options.body: Do not merge this PR until the slot-owner RFC is reopened or replaced with a maintainer-approved design.

options.title: Reject core config change
options.body: Close this direction if maintainers want provenance or slot ownership to be solved through another plugin/API design instead of widening `plugins.slots.*`.

recommendation.title: Sponsor after repair
recommendation.body: Keep the direction open, but require a rebase, the listed source fixes, exact-head proof, and explicit maintainer acceptance before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent merged plugin install slot-selection work makes this the closest available history owner for slot activation and config behavior decisions.
